chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Muskān, from Husayn ibn Hammād, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him, 'When I place my face for prostration, my face falls on a stone or something raised; do I turn my face to a level place?' He said, 'Yes, drag your face on the ground without raising it.'

key_terms.جُرَّ وَجْهَكَ: Drag your face, a specific instruction to ensure the forehead remains in contact with the surface rather than lifting it.
key_terms.حَجَر: Stone, used here as an example of an uneven or raised surface during prayer.
key_terms.سُجُود: Prostration, a key act of worship in Islamic prayer where the forehead touches the ground.
key_terms.مُسْتَوٍ: Level or flat, describing the ideal surface for prostration.

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prostration if the prayer mat or ground is uneven or has raised objects?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical nuance of *sujūd* on uneven surfaces, instructing that one should drag the forehead across the surface to ensure full contact rather than lifting it to find a level spot. This ruling emphasizes the importance of physical humility and complete submission (*khushūʿ*) in prayer, ensuring that the forehead touches the ground as a sign of servitude to God, even if the surface is imperfect. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting ritual purity and posture to real-world conditions while maintaining the spiritual essence of the act.
